Lessons.Title: Diagrams and Equations for Word Problems
ExplanationParagraphs: Original 2021 Lesson 18: model word problems using written situations, equations and tape diagrams. Do not reduce this card-sort lesson to unrelated arithmetic drill: pupils must identify the same quantity structures across representations.

Warm-up — Notice and Wonder: Diagrams. Study the part-whole representations described in the original source: a bar with142 and20; four equal parts5; and a bar containing142 plus four equal parts5. Explain which quantity is the total and which is unknown. Teacher reviews source figures.

Activity 1 — Card Sort: Situations, Equations, and Diagrams. The original source includes A–L cards, some containing printed equations and others diagrams. A and F refer to Clare having225 beads, receiving48 and using70:225+48−70=203. C and J show 225−6×10=165 beads remaining. D and L show 225+7×10=295 clips. E and G show225+6×10=285 crayons. I gives225+35+72=332 baseball cards.

Work with a partner: group source situation and equivalent equations, then explain how a bar diagram could show the same original number relationships. Printed image-only cards B, H and K remain teacher-supplied source visuals because their complete pixel content was not verified; do not fabricate their exact letter matching.

Activity 2 — Makes Sense to Me: A Gallery Walk. Solve the teacher-assigned word problem in a group, present a poster with the diagram, operation sequence, result and check, then visit other posters and leave a mathematically specific sticky-note explanation of why a chosen answer makes sense.

The original six figure alt/URL references and student PDF have not been pixel-verified. The independently worded Edulytics scalar checks cover original number relationships, not a certification of artwork, poster quality, teacher discussion or publisher's gated Equation Match Cool-down.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent representations
KeyConcepts.Definition: A situation, equation and tape diagram can encode the same quantities and operations.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Match mathematical relationships, not merely shared numbers.
KeyConcepts.Example: Clare's 225+48−70=203 in both story and equation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Groups as multiplication
KeyConcepts.Definition: Six equal groups of ten represent 6×10.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Identify whether groups are added or removed.

KeyConcepts.Title: Tape diagram
KeyConcepts.Definition: A bar partition represents quantities contributing to the whole.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Keep labels, known quantities and unknown position consistent with story.
KeyConcepts.Example: Elena: a 225 part plus seven 10 parts.

KeyConcepts.Title: Justify a peer solution
KeyConcepts.Definition: Explain why a numerical result and method fit the original situation.
KeyConcepts.Example: Clare203 is less than original225 after net -22.

WorkedExamples.Title: Match Clare's bead story and equation
WorkedExamples.Question: Clare has225, receives48, uses70. What remains?
Steps: Match card A to equation F; review any source picture separately.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare two situations involving six tens
WorkedExamples.Question: What is 225−6×10 versus 225+6×10?
WorkedExamples.Check: The operation must follow the story, despite same numbers.

WorkedExamples.Title: Elena's notebooks
WorkedExamples.Question: Seven notebooks have 10 clips each, plus a box of225. Total?
Steps: Use a bar model with one225 segment and seven 10 segments.
WorkedExamples.Check: Card D maps to equation L.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Match a +6×10 card with a −6×10 story.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Identical values can encode opposite operations.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Track whether items are received or used.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat the diagram as having one fixed artistic layout.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Equivalent independently authored tape models may have different partition drawings.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Validate total, labels and relationship instead of pixels.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Present a poster answer without reasoning.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The 2021 source explicitly asks a peer to explain why an answer makes sense.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Include a model, operation and reasonableness check.

SummaryPoints: Teacher validates visual-only cards B,H,K and gallery walk.
Telling a story, drawing a bar and writing an equation should preserve the same quantities.
No original publisher artwork or gated Cool-down copied.
